> We have recently discovered that the Sabbat and Camarilla political
> systems can potentially wreak havok.

> to vote on it? Or do only the Camarilla vampires have a say?
>

Messages.Author: Nathan Harada
Messages.Body:
> Darin Clisby wrote:

> We have recently discovered that the Sabbat and Camarilla political
> systems can potentially wreak havok.

> For instance, a Praxis Seizue: Miami is called do all the Sabbat get
> to vote on it? Or do only the Camarilla vampires have a say?
>

> If the first option is correct then the Sabbat can dictate who the
> Camarilla may have as Princes...and unlikely event if you take the RP
> angle. But if the Second option were true, then a Camarilla vote deck
> playing against mostly Sabbat players would stand practically
> unopposed...

Sabbat vampires cannot call Praxis Seizures, but may vote on them.
Unless a Sabbat vote states that "Camarilla kindred may not vote on
this action" or someone has played a Closed Session, everyone with
votes can vote on any political action.
Restrictions usually only apply to people calling votes.
The role-playing angle shouldn't apply to the stated rules of
Jyhad/V:TES, meaning vote decks should have enough power to be
workable, even if someone doesn't think that Tzimisce can vote on
Jazz Wentworth seizing power of Seattle.

-Nathan Harada

Messages.Body:

: > playing against mostly Sabbat players would stand practically
: > unopposed...

: Sabbat vampires cannot call Praxis Seizures, but may vote on them.
: Unless a Sabbat vote states that "Camarilla kindred may not vote on
: this action" or someone has played a Closed Session, everyone with
: votes can vote on any political action.

Anyone notice how much more powerful Closed Session is now? If a Sabbat
political deck is having it out with a Camarilla political deck, the
Camarilla voters can shut out their opponents completely. Cool, eh?

: Restrictions usually only apply to people calling votes.

: The role-playing angle shouldn't apply to the stated rules of
: Jyhad/V:TES, meaning vote decks should have enough power to be
: workable, even if someone doesn't think that Tzimisce can vote on
: Jazz Wentworth seizing power of Seattle.

Actually, this does make sense to me. Camarilla power and Sabbat power
are often two completely different issues. The Sabbat tend to rely
on brute force rather than clandestine politics, and the reverse is true
in the Camarilla. Thus, a successful Praxis Seizure is often the result
of a few well-placed favors and well-timed shifts of power. Crusades,
OTOH, are often products of outright fear and violence. The "votes"
held by Camarilla and Sabbat vampires differ in this respect-they repre-
sent different spheres of influence.
So if Jazz Wentworth wants to become Prince of Seattle, he must
be able to persuade the local Primogen that the local Sabbat Cardinal will
not be a problem. In game terms, if Jazz is unable to overcome, say,
the votes of Angelica, the powers that be will not make him a prince.
I think it all adds an interesting dimension to game politics.

: -Nathan Harada

When a vote is called, The acting minion determines which power structure to
use. If it is camarilla, then only members of the camarilla with camarilla
titles can vote. Same goes if the acting minion is antitribu, then only
antitribu may vote. Panders may vote as antitribu as given by LoP. The
priscus apply only to antitribu called votes. It's in the rules. And yes
the target of the votes can be any/all methusalas.

Messages.Author: Justin Grace
Messages.Body:
In article <328A24...@infomatch.com>, Karl Innes
<in...@infomatch.com> writes

Just to add my two cents' worth, whatever happened when we had such
characters as Regina Giovanni, Stefano Giovanni, Saqqaf, Thetmes, and
all other Non-Camarilla vampires with votes?

Wasn't it assumed that non-Camarilla vampires with votes could still
vote on Camarilla votes? You never questioned that - why on earth would
the head of the Giovanni clan want to bother about a peace treaty? Or
the Calif of Alamut with any action concerning the Prince of, say,
London?

The point I'm trying to make is that just because a character has votes,
does not mean that they can only vote on actions that have been called
by a member of the same sect as them. As I see it (this may be a little
wrong, so I apologise), the characters with votes basically have a
little more influence in vampire society in general - Camarilla vamps
know to respect Thetmes, because if they don't, he'll beat the crap out
of them.

Of course, it's not just fear-mongering; Nosferatu get along very well
iwth their antitribu (all things considered), so isn't it likely that
they know each other? And as for the Malkavians and their antitribu...
well, the less said about that the better.

Just because the new expansion figures cards from a different Sect, one
that has been opposed to the Camarilla since it's formation in the
Inquisition, everyone thinks that Camarilla and Sabbat cannot interact
and vote on the same action. (Not including Sabbat-specific votes.)

And always remember the most important rule in V:TES - whevener the
cards contradict the rules, the rules take precedent - if a card does
not specifically say that only Sabbat may vote in this action, then any
vampire can vote in it. The same goes for cards like Justicar cards -
the clan to which they apply obviously wield more power in such a vote -
they are more respected than an outsider with no knowledge of the
workings of the clan.

Oh well, lecture over
--
Justin Grace
